meaning: The MBTA's operating day. Trains running after midnight still count toward the day they started.

Weekday, Saturday, Sunday or holiday. Holidays (listed in board_data.json meta.holidays) are their own type because the MBTA runs a weekend schedule on most of them, so weekday figures leave them out.

Every service date in the window: weekdays, Saturdays, Sundays and holidays. The late-trip, time-over-schedule and long-gap headline numbers are over all days; the gate-entries number is weekdays only.
How long the published schedule gives a train to get from one stop to the next.
Actual time between stops minus scheduled time. Positive means slower than the schedule.

A train run whose actual time between its first and last compared stops was more than 5 minutes longer than scheduled. The same 5-minute rule applies on every line, so long lines are more exposed to it.
For one train run, the sum of (actual minus scheduled) time over its compared stop-to-stop segments. Averaged per trip, not per stop.
Total excess time divided by total scheduled run time. Compares lines of different length on an equal footing.
The gap between one train leaving a station and the next train on the same line leaving it.
A wait more than 1.5 times the scheduled gap, e.g. 12+ minutes when trains are due every 8.
A train leaving a station less than half the scheduled gap after the train before it.
Share of gaps between half and 1.5 times the scheduled gap.
Fare-gate entries at a station, from MBTA's published counts. Each entry is counted once, on one line. One person can make several entries a day, so entries are not riders.
MBTA time-of-day bands from its Service Delivery Policy, e.g. AM Peak 7:00-8:59.

For each station, line and time of day: average gated entries times the share of train departures that came after a long gap, summed. An estimate of how many entries happen during long gaps, not a head count of people who waited.
